House Democrat Leadership Defends Ilhan Omar After Raid: 'Deeply Disturbing' that Trump's 'Violent Mass Deportation Machine' Raided Her Home

House Democrats defended Somali-born Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-MN) after the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) conducted a pre-dawn raid of her home Monday, characterizing it as a "violent mass deportation machine" and calling it "deeply disturbing."
The post House Democrat Leadership Defends Ilhan Omar After Raid: ‘Deeply Disturbing’ that Trump’s ‘Violent Mass Deportation Machine’ Raided Her Home appeared first on Breitbart.

Actual Article Body:
House Democrats defended Somali-born Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-MN) after the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) conducted a pre-dawn raid of her home Monday, characterizing it as a “violent mass deportation machine” and calling it “deeply disturbing.”

House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries, Whip Katherine Clark, and Caucus Chair Pete Aguilar issued a joint statement after the raid, which a Department of Justice spokesperson confirmed was part of an “ongoing federal investigation.” According to reports, more specifically, the raid was part of an ongoing criminal fraud investigation into Omar’s immigration paperwork.

“The Trump administration’s raid on Congresswoman Ilhan Omar’s home is deeply disturbing and raises serious questions about the continued corrupt weaponization of the federal government against Donald Trump’s adversaries,” the Democrats said in their joint statement, failing to address the irony of their word choice given the left’s well-documented cases of weaponizing the federal government against their political enemies.

“For years, Donald Trump and far-right extremists have relentlessly targeted Congresswoman Omar with vile personal attacks and baseless accusations,” the Democrats continued. “Now, less than 30 days until the midterm election, his violent mass deportation machine has descended upon the home of a duly elected Member of Congress and her family.”

They added, “The American people deserve transparency, and we will deliver full accountability for the rogue abuse of power from the Department of Homeland Security and Department of Justice.”

Omar also released a brief statement on X, claiming to be a victim of the Trump administration, although her account has limited the accounts that can reply to it.

“I’m ok. Make no mistake: this is an attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement. For ten years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns. This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation,” she said, adding, “I will not be silenced.”

As Breitbart News has detailed, Omar has long come under fire for her anti-America statements and questionable immigration history, the latter of which has caught the attention of the commander-in-chief.

“Somalia, where you have a Congressman goes around telling everybody about our Constitution, yet she supposedly came into our country by marrying her brother,” President Donald Trump told reporters aboard Air Force One last year. “Well, if that’s true, she shouldn’t be a Congressman, and we should throw her the hell out of our country.”

Last year, Omar said America is becoming “one of the worst countries” in the world.

“You have states’ rights being disregarded. So, you know, the constitutional crisis that’s being created in front of our eyes, and the same week where we have a president who has deployed the military who are trained to kill our enemies, not Americans, but our enemies, are in our streets. It’s the same week that we are going to have a military parade,” she complained last year, referencing the parade celebrating the 250th anniversary of the U.S. Army.

“I mean, I grew up in a dictatorship and I don’t even remember ever witnessing anything like that. To have a democracy, a beacon of hope for the world to now be turned into one of the, you know, one of the worst countries,” she continued, falsely claiming that the U.S. military is in the streets “without any regard for people’s constitutional rights” and accusing President Trump of propping himself up like a “failed dictator.”

New White House press secretary a "devoted fan" of Trump and MAGA

Katie Zacharia worked for one of Trump's companies and raised her profile appearing on conservative-leaning talk shows. She also amplified right-wing conspiracy theories. Now she'll be the president's chief spokesperson.

Actual Article Body:
Brian Mann

Katie Zacharia, pictured on December 14, 2025 in Franklin, Tennessee, starts her tenure as White House press secretary.
                
                    
                    Terry Wyatt/Getty Images North America
                    
                
                hide caption

President Trump's new White House press secretary Katie Zacharia is expected to take the podium on Tuesday for her first press briefing. Zacharia steps in as Trump's chief spokesperson at a moment when his popularity has fallen to record lows and Republicans are scrambling to limit potential losses in the midterm elections.

The Trump administration is also engaged in a legal battle with the press corps that work to cover Trump. Last month, the White House restricted access by CNN, MS NOW and Politico, news organizations that Trump views as unfriendly. The Justice Department has since launched an investigation into the five television networks that share pool video coverage of Trump.

In a post on social media, Zacharia, an attorney and a mother of four, offered no hint of the challenges ahead. She described her new job as the "honor of a lifetime" and praised Trump's policies. "His confidence is a true privilege, and his leadership is a blessing to this country," Zacharia wrote on Friday.

In naming Zacharia, Trump praised her longstanding personal loyalty. "She has an unblemished record of support, and has been a loyal and brilliant supporter, right from the beginning," Trump said. "She is, likewise, a devoted fan and member of MAGA!"

Zacharia, 41, a graduate of Pepperdine Caruso School of Law, has worked for a number of conservative organizations, according to her online resume. She served on the advisory board for an anti-abortion group called The White Rose Resistance that took its name from Christian students who challenged the Nazis. White Rose says it's working to counter "the same evils, the same apathy" faced by opponents of the Nazi regime.

More recently, Zacharia has served as a communications advisor for the Trump Media & Technology Group, the firm that operates Trump's Truth Social platform. She has also been a frequent pro-Trump commentator on conservative outlets including Fox News and Newsmax.

During an appearance in August on the network Real America's Voice, Zacharia weighed in on the Lindsay Clancy murder trial, arguing that "toxic feminism" had skewed the public's view of the case. Clancy was charged with killing her three children. The 5-week trial ended in a mistrial after sparking a national conversation over postpartum depression.

"This started with the advocation of abortion," Zacharia said. "When women are championing the death and murder and the ability to murder their children from conception all the way through, when does humanity begin and end?"

Zacharia has also used her social media posts to amplify right-wing conspiracy theories, including claims that Democratic leaders took part in pedophile rings. In one post from 2022, she described former Democratic White House chief of staff John Podesta as "Pedo Podesta." That same year she shared a post from a far-right commentator who claimed Democrats "want to mask and rape your children."

NPR asked the White House for comment on the posts, which were first uncovered by the online progressive media site, Popular Information. Administration officials responded in an email by praising Zacharia without addressing her social media comments.

After being named to serve as White House press secretary, Zacharia drew praise from other administration officials. FBI director Kash Patel described her as "sharp, fearless" and someone who "knows what it means to stand for the American people."

Karoline Leavitt, who held the press secretary post until August before stepping down, also praised Zacharia. "I have no doubt Katie will do great work for President Trump and our country," she said on X.

In an appearance on Fox News on Saturday, Zacharia boosted Trump's controversial plan to import Russian diesel fuel, which has drawn bipartisan criticism. She also praised Trump's efforts to rally GOP support ahead of the November vote, while suggesting congressional Republicans may be to blame for any losses.

"President Trump has made the case and delivered historic results. I would have loved to see more from our congressional Republicans and Senate," she said.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
New White House press secretary Katie Zacharia spotted as Trump departs for Ohio rally – with Jake Paul and Jon Gruden

Zacharia, who is not accompanying the president to the Ohio rally, is slated to deliver her first White House press briefing on Tuesday.

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

White House press secretary Katie Zacharia was spotted Monday, her first official day on the job, as President Trump boarded his helicopter to head to a rally with Jake Paul and Jon Gruden.

Zacharia watched from a distance as Trump gaggled with reporters for several minutes before boarding Marine One. The president is traveling to Youngstown, Ohio, for a midterm election rally for Republican candidates.

Zacharia is not accompanying the president on the trip. She’s slated to deliver her first press briefing on Tuesday.

Paul, a professional boxer and influencer, and Gruden, a Barstool Sports commentator and Super Bowl-winning NFL head coach, joined Trump on Marine One and are expected to appear at the Buckeye State rally. Paul was donning a red “America is Back” hat.

Sen. Jon Husted (R-Ohio) and Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy are among the slate of candidates Trump has endorsed in Ohio.

Husted is locked in a tight race with former Sen. Sherrod Brown (D-Ohio), while Ramaswamy is vying against physician and former public health official Amy Acton.

Gruden, a native of Sandusky, Ohio, was a college teammate of Husted’s at the University of Dayton.

The former Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Las Vegas Raiders head coach fired up the crowd at an Ohio rally for Husted, which Trump also spoke at, earlier this month.

Paul is also an Ohio native and appeared alongside Trump at a Kentucky event – just across the border – earlier this year.

Trump predicted the boxer and social media star “will be, in the not too distant future, running for political office,” at the Hebron, Ky., event.
